reviewed_by: Delegated coding agent static review against live Binary Ninja 6.0.10601 MCP (retail PE view_1), radare2 6.2.0 CFG and angr 10.0.4.post1 CFGFast on retail igi.exe; candidate source read from this worktree. No game process was executed and no runtime behavior is claimed.
review_basis: Retail 0x004A9CE5 was re-disassembled, re-decompiled and re-CFG'd through the live Binary Ninja view, independently recovered with radare2 6.2.0 and angr 10.0.4.post1 CFGFast. The candidate is scripts/GameNatives/camera/004A9CE5-Camera_ApplyLineFilter_18.cpp at sha256 cd683e84639210ea220bc4436b9512bde7e0343dba68a470aee6496642d00754 (recorded implementation.signature: long double __fastcall Camera_ApplyLineFilter_18(int32_t param_1, double* param_2);). The evidence artifact digests are bound in this review.

retail_function.name: Camera_ApplyLineFilter_18
retail_function.summary: Three blocks 0x4A9CE5-0x4A9D27: read the qword at EDX; if the exponent word (&0x7FF00000) is not 0x7FF00000, load it with fld and retn. Otherwise build a 10-byte extended value from the two dwords (shld/shl 0xB), OR 0x7FFF0000 into the high word, `fld tword [esp]`, and return it in st0.

candidate_function.signature: long double __fastcall Camera_ApplyLineFilter_18(int32_t param_1, double* param_2);
candidate_function.summary: __fload_withFB(int context, double* arg2) reproduces the exponent test, the 0x7FFF0000 OR, the shld/shl pair, and the dead `*(arg2 + 4);` load, but returns the integer `(entity_val << 0xb)` instead of the 10-byte extended value.

divergences: NaN path returns a 32-bit shifted integer instead of the 80-bit extended value loaded by `fld tword [esp]` (0x4A9D19); the returned mantissa/exponent are wrong.
The candidate's declared long double return is not produced on either path (`return *arg2` vs `return (entity_val << 0xB)`).
candidate_comparison.statement: Divergences are listed above; by contract they keep the record at TRANSCRIBED or lower.

checks.name: function_identity
checks.detail: Retail entry 0x004A9CE5 is recovered by all three tools; the address-bound implementation is scripts/GameNatives/camera/004A9CE5-Camera_ApplyLineFilter_18.cpp (sha256 cd683e84639210ea220bc4436b9512bde7e0343dba68a470aee6496642d00754). Three blocks 0x4A9CE5-0x4A9D27: read the qword at EDX; if the exponent word (&0x7FF00000) is not 0x7FF00000, load it with fld and retn. Otherwise build a 10-byte extended value from the two dwords (shld/shl 0xB), OR 0x7FFF0000 into the high word, `fld tword [esp]`, and return it in st0. Candidate: __fload_withFB(int context, double* arg2) reproduces the exponent test, the 0x7FFF0000 OR, the shld/shl pair, and the dead `*(arg2 + 4);` load, but returns the integer `(entity_val << 0xb)` instead of the 10-byte extended value.

checks.name: abi_and_signature
checks.detail: Retail is __fastcall (EDX = qword pointer) and returns a long double in st0; BN models `long double __fastcall(int32_t arg1, double* arg2)`. The candidate declares `long double __fastcall` but its return statement yields a 32-bit integer expression, so the st0 result is not produced.

checks.name: argument_mapping
checks.detail: EDX carries the qword pointer in both; the candidate's `arg2` is the __fastcall second argument (EDX).

checks.name: control_flow_shape
checks.detail: Binary Ninja and radare2 agree on 3 blocks / 2 edges (similarity 1.000); angr CFGFast recovers 3 blocks with has_unresolved_jumps=false.

checks.name: memory_layout_and_access
checks.detail: Both read the two dwords at arg2 and build the 10-byte value on the stack; the candidate keeps the dead high-word reload.

checks.name: return_and_error_paths
checks.detail: Retail returns the NaN-fixed 80-bit value through st0 (`fld tword [esp]`); the candidate returns `(entity_val << 0xB)` as a 32-bit int zero-extended into a long double result slot, so the returned bit pattern is wrong on the NaN path.

checks.name: floating_point_semantics
checks.detail: The extended-precision load (`fld tword`) that distinguishes the NaN path is not represented in the candidate's return expression.

signature_comparison.rationale: Binary Ninja reports "long double __fastcall(int32_t arg1, double* arg2)" at 0x004A9CE5; radare2 recovers "fcn.004a9ce5 ();". Both tools place the entry at 0x004A9CE5 and agree on the stack/register word count and cleanup; the difference is the level of type/argument-name detail, not the call frame. Candidate declaration: long double __fastcall Camera_ApplyLineFilter_18(int32_t param_1, double* param_2);. The candidate declaration is separately recorded as divergent below and does not satisfy the retail ABI.

limitations: No game process was executed; this review is static (live Binary Ninja, radare2 CFG, angr CFGFast) plus the candidate source.
The candidate defines __fload_withFB, not the catalog name Camera_ApplyLineFilter_18.
